summary: Full read of 20 SEC whistleblower award orders (19 Feb - 17 May 2021); pages without a text layer (91253 pp. 2 and 4, 91808 p. 4) were OCRed. Adds 17 case rows: 16 denial rows (other claimants, contested and uncontested, and related-action claims denied in the same orders) and 1 award row (Release No. 91427, Claimant 2, 10%; the existing combined row is suggested to become Claimant 1's 20%). Suggested corrections add to each existing award row how the claimant qualified, contests, reductions for reporting delay, the 30% presumption, Rule 21F-9(e) waivers, insider and internal-reporting facts, and fix one wrong qualifier (91903 Claimant 2: "approximately", not "over"). No statistics, new rules or new events beyond what is already recorded.

Tip submitted over a year after the investigation opened; concerned a competitor of the company; claimed news articles based on his/her information prompted the company's internal review. Commission rejects "alternative circumstances" outside the three prongs of Rule 21F-4(c), following Release No. 89551 (13 Aug 2020).

suggested_corrections.value: Exchange Act Release No. 91164, File No. 2021-26. Listed on the SEC Final Orders page as "Award Order (PDF)" (Feb. 19, 2021). Whistleblowers awarded: 1. Tip about a fraudulent reporting scheme prompted the opening of the investigation; Claimant gave additional critical documents, helped identify key documents and witnesses, and raised concerns internally first. Percentage, covered action and sanctions redacted. A second claimant was denied (separate row).
Award for a tip about a fraudulent reporting scheme that prompted the investigation; claimant had first raised concerns internally.

Exchange Act Release No. 91183, File No. 2021-28. Listed on the SEC Final Orders page as "Award Order (PDF)" (Feb. 23, 2021). Whistleblowers awarded: 1. Amount as printed: "more than": lower bound. Award amount and percentage are as recommended by the Claims Review Staff and adopted by the Commission unless the order says otherwise. Award is for related actions only (brought by the US Department of Justice); Claimant had earlier received an award in the Commission covered action. One related action is a DOJ agreement with a company (type redacted, "*** PA"), counted as a related action under the rule amendments effective 7 Dec 2020. Not contested. Information on an ongoing fraud; large amount returned to harmed investors; Claimant travelled at own expense to be interviewed by DOJ. Percentage and sanctions redacted.
Award on DOJ related actions (one a prosecution agreement with a company, newly eligible under the 2020 rule amendments) for information on an ongoing fraud.

Exchange Act Release No. 91206, File No. 2021-29. Listed on the SEC Final Orders page as "Award Order (PDF)" (Feb. 25, 2021). Whistleblowers awarded: 1. Amount as printed: "over": lower bound. Award amount and percentage are as recommended by the Claims Review Staff and adopted by the Commission unless the order says otherwise. Award covers both the Commission covered action and related actions by another authority (name redacted). Not contested. Claimant met the new Rule 21F-9(e) TCR waiver: filed a Form TCR within (redacted) days of learning of the requirement. Information during an ongoing investigation expedited it and contributed to several charges; declaration and repeated assistance; Commission shut down an ongoing scheme against retail investors and obtained emergency relief. Percentage and sanctions redacted.
Award on a covered action and related actions; late Form TCR excused under Rule 21F-9(e); helped shut down an ongoing scheme against retail investors.

Exchange Act Release No. 91207, File No. 2021-30. Listed on the SEC Final Orders page as "Award Order (PDF)" (Feb. 25, 2021). Whistleblowers awarded: 1. Amount as printed: "over": lower bound. Award amount and percentage are as recommended by the Claims Review Staff and adopted by the Commission unless the order says otherwise. Not contested. Claimant did not file a Form TCR within 30 days of first contacting the Commission but got the Rule 21F-9(e) waiver (TCR filed within 30 days of learning of the requirement). Interview and documents gave important evidence of false and misleading statements to investors; helped return millions of dollars to harmed investors. Percentage, covered action and sanctions redacted; several redacted paragraphs and footnotes 2-4.
Award for evidence of false statements to investors; late Form TCR excused under Rule 21F-9(e).

Exchange Act Release No. 91225, File No. 2021-31. Listed on the SEC Final Orders page as "Award Order (PDF)" (March 1, 2021). Whistleblowers awarded: 2. Amount as printed: "over": lower bound. Award amount and percentage are as recommended by the Claims Review Staff and adopted by the Commission unless the order says otherwise. Two claimants (Claimant 1 and Claimant 2), equal split of the same (redacted) percentage each, on a covered action (judicial and administrative actions treated as one) and a related action by another agency (name redacted); aggregate award "over $500,000" so far. Not contested. Both tips caused the swift opening of the Commission's and the other agency's investigations; substantial ongoing assistance; ongoing fraud. Disgorgement deemed satisfied by the related action's order: only amounts actually collected count, no double counting. Percentages and sanctions redacted.
Equal award to two claimants whose tips opened the SEC's and another agency's investigations into an ongoing fraud (covered and related action).

Exchange Act Release No. 91253, File No. 2021-32. Listed on the SEC Final Orders page as "Award and Denial Orders (PDF)" (March 4, 2021). Whistleblowers awarded: 2. Amount as printed: "over": lower bound. Award amount and percentage are as recommended by the Claims Review Staff and adopted by the Commission unless the order says otherwise. Joint award to Claimants 1 and 2, who jointly filed the tip and Forms WB-APP; paid 50% each unless they ask for a different split. Not contested. Joint tip caused staff to open the investigation (settled administrative proceeding against a company); misconduct abroad that would have been hard to detect; some charges concerned wider misconduct than they reported. Denials: Claimants 3-10 (uncontested) and Claimants 11 and 12 (contested) (separate rows). Percentage, company and sanctions redacted. Pages 2 and 4 are images (read by OCR).
Joint award to two claimants whose tip opened an investigation into misconduct abroad; ten other claimants denied.

Claimant first reported concerns internally to the employer; information caused staff to open an investigation; multiple written submissions, identified potential witnesses, met staff several times. Award to a claimant who reported internally to the employer and whose information opened the investigation; related-action claim denied.

Exchange Act Release No. 91332, File No. 2021-34. Listed on the SEC Final Orders page as "Award Order (PDF)" (March 16, 2021). Whistleblowers awarded: 1. Award at the statutory maximum under the Rule 21F-6(c) presumption (maximum award $5 million or less, no negative factors, Rule 21F-16 not triggered; assistance more than limited). Information contributed to opening the investigation and significantly contributed to the action; significant ongoing assistance and numerous documents. No other claimants.
Maximum 30% award under the new presumption for awards of $5 million or less.

Exchange Act Release No. 91426, File No. 2021-35. Listed on the SEC Final Orders page as "Award Order (PDF)" (March 29, 2021). Whistleblowers awarded: 1. Amount as printed: "over": lower bound. Amount as printed: "over": lower bound (the redaction splits the phrase). Award on a covered action and a related action by another authority (name redacted); the covered action's sanctions were deemed satisfied in the related action, no double counting. Not contested. Insider who reported internally to the employer; the information went via the employer to another authority, which referred it to the SEC, prompting the investigation; Claimant faxed a tip within 120 days, so the Rule 21F-4(b)(7) safe harbor dates the submission to the internal report (also Rule 21F-4(c)(3)). Met staff in person; actions shut down an ongoing fraudulent scheme. Percentages and sanctions redacted.
Award to an employee who reported internally first; the 120-day safe harbor dated the tip to the internal report; covered and related action.

Exchange Act Release No. 91649, File No. 2021-41. Listed on the SEC Final Orders page as "Award Order (PDF)" (April 23, 2021). Whistleblowers awarded: 1. Amount as printed: "approximately". Maximum 30% award under the presumption on a covered action and related judicial actions; prompt tip opened the investigation.

Exchange Act Release No. 91808, File No. 2021-45. Listed on the SEC Final Orders page as "Award Orders (PDF)" (May 10, 2021). Separate award amounts per claimant in one order: this row is the amount stated for Claimant 1 (claimants numbered in the order the amounts appear). Amount as printed: "nearly": upper bound. Claimant 1: award on two covered actions (settled administrative proceedings against a financial services firm and a second respondent; sanctions fully collected, amounts redacted); same percentage in each (redacted). Contested the percentage, asking for 30% and no award for Claimant 2; Commission kept the CRS recommendation after an additional staff declaration. Claimant 1's tip was the initial source of the investigation, years before Claimant 2's; extensive ongoing assistance; persistent efforts to remedy the issues while suffering hardships; "the main source of information". Three other claimants denied (separate row).
Largest award in the order to the claimant whose tip, years earlier, started the investigation of a financial services firm; contested and upheld.

Exchange Act Release No. 91808, File No. 2021-45. Listed on the SEC Final Orders page as "Award Orders (PDF)" (May 10, 2021). Separate award amounts per claimant in one order: this row is the amount stated for Claimant 2 (claimants numbered in the order the amounts appear). Amount as printed: "more than": lower bound. Claimant 2: award on the same two covered actions. Contested the percentage; Commission kept it. Recent insider and first-hand witness who reported several years after Claimant 1; award reduced for unreasonable reporting delay (several years after becoming aware), by less than otherwise because Claimant 2 had passed information to Claimant 1 knowing it went to the SEC. Commission rejected Claimant 1's request to reduce Claimant 2's award for culpability (no evidence of culpable conduct in the transactions at issue). Percentage redacted.
Smaller award to a recent insider who reported years after the first whistleblower; reduced for unreasonable reporting delay.

Award for new information that opened an investigation leading directly to charges against a company; two other claimants denied.

Exchange Act Release No. 91896, File No. 2021-47. Listed on the SEC Final Orders page as "Award Order (PDF)" (May 14, 2021). Whistleblowers awarded: 1. Maximum 30% award under the presumption for alerting the SEC to an ongoing fraud; investor distributions count as collected sanctions.

Exchange Act Release No. 91902, File No. 2021-48. Listed on the SEC Final Orders page as "Award and Denial Orders (PDF)" (May 17, 2021). Whistleblowers awarded: 2. Amount as printed: "almost": upper bound. Award amount and percentage are as recommended by the Claims Review Staff and adopted by the Commission unless the order says otherwise. Joint award to Claimants 1 and 2 (paid 50% each unless they jointly ask otherwise). Claimant 1 contested, arguing they were not joint whistleblowers (an unwritten team agreement, with a third person, that Claimant 1 would file and split any award); the Commission held they had presented themselves as a team with the same counsel. After Claimant 1's response the CRS raised the joint percentage (from and to percentages redacted). New but limited information years after the investigation opened (significant contribution, Rule 21F-4(c)(2)); met staff on three days; both had reported internally; millions returned to harmed investors. Claimant 3 (contested) and a fourth claimant (no response) denied (separate rows).
Joint award, increased on reconsideration, to two internal reporters whose limited later information advanced an existing investigation; dispute over the joint split rejected.

Exchange Act Release No. 91903, File No. 2021-49. Listed on the SEC Final Orders page as "Award and Denial Orders (PDF)" (May 17, 2021). Separate award amounts per claimant in one order: this row is the amount stated for Claimant 1 (claimants numbered in the order the amounts appear). Amount as printed: "approximately". Claimant 1: contested the percentage; kept. Covered action = a settled proceeding against a company plus one against an individual, treated as one. Tip came about a year after the investigation began and contributed only to the much smaller Individual Action; reduced for reporting delay (more than five years after learning of the violations); staff found Claimant 2's information more valuable; Claimant 1 had reported internally and suffered retaliation, harassment, wrongful termination and financial hardship (as claimed). Related-action claim denied (separate row). Percentage redacted.
Smaller award to a claimant whose late tip (over five years) helped only the action against an individual; claimant reported internally and suffered retaliation.

Exchange Act Release No. 91903, File No. 2021-49. Listed on the SEC Final Orders page as "Award and Denial Orders (PDF)" (May 17, 2021). Separate award amounts per claimant in one order: this row is the amount stated for Claimant 2 (claimants numbered in the order the amounts appear). Amount as printed: "over": lower bound. Correction to the note above: the order prints "approximately $3,750,000", not "over". Claimant 2: preliminarily denied as not voluntary (requests for information came first), but on reconsideration new evidence showed Claimant 2 had given the same information to another authority before any request (Rule 21F-4(a)(2)), so the CRS found Claimant 2 eligible and gave the larger award. Information shortly after the investigation began significantly contributed to both the Company and Individual Actions; no negative factors. Percentage redacted.
Larger award, after an initial denial was reversed on reconsideration, to a claimant whose earlier report to another authority made the information voluntary.
